_meta.about: Per-city content for the 'Whose city is it?' on-ramp game. Every number is sourced from the atlas's own data — function_control_matrix.md (functions city/state, of 18) and service_providers.json + governance.json (decided_by over the 15 core services, corporation-type = city-decided, all else = state). Editorial reveal copy is authored; the figures are not.
_meta.decided_by_rule: Of the 15 core municipal services, count provider 'type'=='corporation' as city-decided; state_board / state_dept / private / spv as not-city-decided; 'na' (service absent) excluded from the denominator. This is the exact rule that reproduces Ahmedabad's stored decided_by (10/15 = 67%).

ahmedabad.name: Ahmedabad

r1.verdict: Ahmedabad keeps more than most — and it’s still only half.
r1.body: It held on to its water and fire when other cities lost them. But town planning, housing, slums & urban poverty, the environment — handed to state bodies you never voted for (AUDA draws the blueprint, GWSSB owns the bulk water). Your council sweeps the streets; the state draws the map.
r1.source: Source: AMC function-control matrix, 18 Twelfth-Schedule functions · Art. 243W (“may, by law, endow”).

r2.verdict: The state keeps it. Your city legally cannot tax you.
r2.body: Stamp duty — the tax on every property sale — goes to Gujarat, not AMC. Your city has no constitutional power to tax (Art. 243X): it lives on fees, fines, and grants handed down from above. The one levy it does collect, property tax, it under-collects — a quiet subsidy to whoever owns the most land.
r2.source: Source: Constitution Art. 243X (no municipal taxation entry); property-tax & stamp-duty regime, rent-capture dossier.

r3.setup: You elected 192 councillors. So who actually runs the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, day to day?
r3.choiceAsub: The elected head of the council
r3.choiceBsub: Not on any ballot I saw
r3.verdict: A man you never voted for: the Municipal Commissioner.
r3.body: Banchhanidhi Pani — an IAS officer appointed by the state, not elected by you — runs AMC day to day. Your BJP council (160 of 192 seats) sets policy; the commissioner and the state hold the executive. Of your 15 core services, 5 aren’t city-decided — electricity is private, the metro and BRTS are state SPVs, and town planning is AUDA’s. (Your police — city and traffic — were never AMC’s: police is a State subject in every Indian city, run by Gujarat.)
r3.source: Source: AMC governance record (commissioner B. Pani, IAS; council BJP 160/192, Apr 2026); service-decider tally 10/15 city.

ahmedabad.end: Ahmedabad is the strongest city we mapped — and it still only half-owns its own government.

bengaluru.name: Bengaluru

r1.verdict: Bengaluru lost even its water and fire to the state.
r1.body: By the constitutional count your city runs just 7 of 18 functions — water went to the BWSSB, planning to the BDA, fire to the state, boards you never voted for. And since the 2025 GBA reorganisation, even those 7 no longer sit with one elected city: they’re split across five corporations, under a Chief-Minister-chaired apex (the GBA) that holds the planning and coordination above them. The number holds at 7; the control is thinner than it looks.
r1.source: Source: function-control matrix, 18 Twelfth-Schedule functions (constitutional count — carve-out cities run 7/18). Post-2025 the same 7 are fragmented across 5 City Corporations under the CM-chaired GBA — Greater Bengaluru Governance Act (Karnataka Act 36 of 2025).

r2.verdict: The state keeps it. Your city legally cannot tax you.
r2.body: Stamp duty — the tax on every property sale — goes to Karnataka, not the city. No city in India has the constitutional power to tax (Art. 243X); Bengaluru lives on fees, fines, and grants handed down from above, while the land it sits on makes others rich.
r2.source: Source: Constitution Art. 243X (no municipal taxation entry); property-tax & stamp-duty regime.

r3.setup: The last time you elected a city council was 2015. So who runs Bengaluru now?
r3.choiceBsub: I haven’t voted for the city in years
r3.verdict: No mayor. No council. An administrator the state appointed.
r3.body: You last voted for a Bengaluru council in 2015; that term ended in 2020 and was never renewed. Then in 2025 the state abolished BBMP altogether, replacing it with an unelected Greater Bengaluru Authority and five corporations no one has voted for. The city is run by M. Maheshwar Rao, an IAS administrator. The state also runs your water, sewerage, power, buses and even your fire brigade — 8 of your 14 services aren’t city-decided. (Police, as everywhere in India, was always the state’s.)
r3.source: Source: Greater Bengaluru Governance Act (Karnataka Act 36 of 2025, in force 15 May 2025) abolishing BBMP; Bengaluru governance record (administrator M. Maheshwar Rao, IAS); last municipal election 2015, fresh polls pending; service-decider tally 6/14 city.

bengaluru.end: Ahmedabad you half-own. Bengaluru you don’t own at all — you haven’t even voted for it since 2015.
